AA_FalconXUSDC is the senior ("AA") tranche receipt token issued by Pareto Credit for
the FalconX USDC private credit vault. Depositors supply USDC which is lent to FalconX,
the institutional digital-asset prime broker, through a structured credit facility. The
AA tranche holds the most-senior claim on repayment and accrues a fixed rate over USDC.

[Pareto Credit](https://pareto.credit/) (formerly Idle DAO's senior/junior tranche
infrastructure) operates programmable institutional credit vaults on Ethereum. The
FalconX Credit Vault channels USDC deposits into a structured credit facility for
[FalconX](https://www.falconx.io/), a leading digital-asset prime broker that
finances hedge funds, trading firms, and other institutional counterparties.

## Tranche structure

The vault is split into two tranches via Pareto's Collateralised Debt Obligation (CDO)
architecture, curated by M11 Credit:

- **AA tranche (AA_FalconXUSDC)** — senior class; receives principal and interest first,
  carries lower yield but highest capital protection.
- **BB tranche (BB_FalconXUSDC)** — junior/equity class; absorbs first losses in exchange
  for higher yield.

The CDO contract (`0x433D5B175148dA32Ffe1e1A37a939E1b7e79be4d`) mints both tranche
tokens, with USDC (`0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48`) as the sole
underlying asset. NAV accrues continuously; redemptions follow monthly mechanics
governed by the FalconX credit facility terms.

## Composability

After the vault crossed $135 million in deposits, Pareto enabled AA_FalconXUSDC as
collateral on [Morpho](https://morpho.org/) (Steakhouse market) so holders can borrow
additional USDC. Gauntlet and Aera Finance also offer a levered RWA loop strategy using
these tokens.

## Risk profile

The AA tranche is protected by the junior tranche equity buffer and transaction-level
collateralisation, plus a real-time risk engine. Reserve attestations and quarterly
ISAE 3000 assurance reports are published by the protocol. Pharos Watch publishes an
independent risk profile for the token.

Acala Dollar (aUSD) is the native decentralised stablecoin of the Acala network on Polkadot. It is overcollateralised and multi-collateral-backed, designed for cross-chain DeFi. aUSD suffered a depeg exploit in August 2022 and has very limited usage today.

aUSD was its native decentralised stablecoin, issued via the Honzon protocol using an overcollateralised
CDP (collateralised debt position) model backed by multiple cross-chain assets including DOT, LDOT, and iBTC.

## The August 2022 exploit

On 14 August 2022, a misconfiguration in the newly deployed iBTC/aUSD liquidity pool allowed 16 addresses
to erroneously mint approximately 3.022 billion aUSD from thin air. The price of aUSD collapsed from ~$1.03
to $0.009 within minutes — a 99% depeg. Acala entered error mode, pausing most network operations.
Following emergency governance votes, approximately 2.97 billion of the erroneously minted tokens were
traced and 1.29 billion were burnt, allowing the peg to partially recover to ~$0.93 before further burns
restored near-parity.

## Status

aUSD never fully recovered market confidence after the exploit. Circulating supply and on-chain usage
remain negligible.

Basis Cash was an anonymous, community-run implementation of the [Basis](https://basis.io/) algorithmic

- Field: users lend Bean to the protocol in exchange for Pods (future Bean), providing peg-recovery incentive

BOLD is the native stablecoin of [Liquity V2](https://www.liquity.org/), launched in 2024. It is the
successor to LUSD and maintains the same core principles of full decentralisation and immutability.
BOLD is rated A- by Bluechip, making it one of the highest-rated decentralised stablecoins.

## Mechanism

- Overcollateralised CDP model: backed exclusively by WETH, wstETH, and rETH
- Minimum collateral ratio: 110% (no stability fee; instead users set their own interest rate)
- Always redeemable at face value: 1 BOLD = $1 of collateral
- No governance: protocol is immutable and fully on-chain
- 100% of protocol revenue distributed to BOLD stakers and liquidity providers
- Stability Pool absorbs liquidations

- [Liquity V2 documentation](https://docs.liquity.org/)

BitVault USD (bvUSD) is an overcollateralised CDP stablecoin by BitVault, a Liquity V2 fork on the Katana chain. It is backed by WBTC and WETH collateral with institutional-only bulk minting.

bvUSD is issued by [BitVault](https://bitvault.finance/), a [Liquity V2](https://www.liquity.org/) fork
deployed primarily on [Katana](https://katana.network/), a DeFi-focused chain incubated by Polygon Labs and GSR.

## Mechanism

- Overcollateralised CDP model backed by WBTC and WETH
- Initial LTV of 40%, up to 75% thereafter
- Only whitelisted institutional borrowers can mint bvUSD in bulk; retail users mint via other stablecoins
- Stability Pool absorbs liquidations (same architecture as Liquity)
- Contracts are immutable once deployed

## Yield

sbvUSD is the staked/yield-bearing version of bvUSD, where yield comes from delta-neutral
institutional trading strategies (arbitrage, market-making) executed by [GSR](https://www.gsr.io/).

## Status

Early-stage, launched on Katana on 19 June 2025. Raised $2M pre-seed from GSR, Gemini, and Auros.
Not independently tracked on DeFiLlama or CoinGecko.

BYUSD is a stablecoin issued by Bybit, the cryptocurrency exchange. It is currently deployed on Berachain and is part of Bybit's Web3 stablecoin initiative. Details about reserves and redemption mechanisms are limited to exchange disclosures.

BYUSD is a fiat-backed stablecoin issued by [Bybit](https://www.bybit.com/), one of the world's
largest centralised cryptocurrency exchanges. Each BYUSD token is pegged 1:1 to the US dollar and
backed by Bybit's fiat reserves. The token is currently deployed on [Berachain](https://berachain.com/),
where it serves as a liquidity asset within the ecosystem.

## Mechanism

BYUSD is a centralised, fiat-collateralised stablecoin in the same category as USDT and USDC.
Bybit maintains reserves verified through its ongoing [Proof of Reserves](https://www.bybit.com/app/user/proof-of-reserve)
programme, audited by Hacken, with reported reserve ratios consistently above 100%.

On Berachain, BYUSD can be used as accepted collateral to mint HONEY (Berachain's native stablecoin)
through the HoneySwap dApp. Deep BYUSD liquidity pools also help anchor HONEY's peg by providing
low-slippage redemption routes.

## Key properties

- Centralised issuance by Bybit exchange
- 1:1 USD backing with fiat reserves
- Monthly/regular Proof of Reserves audits via Hacken
- Currently deployed on Berachain; usable as collateral for HONEY minting

## Sources

- [Stablecoins on Berachain — Berachain Blog](https://blog.berachain.com/blog/stablecoins-on-berachain)
- [CoinGecko — BYUSD](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/byusd)

cDAI is the Compound V2 protocol's interest-bearing token representing DAI supplied to the Compound lending pool on Ethereum. It accrues interest automatically as borrowers pay interest on DAI loans. cDAI was one of the earliest DeFi yield-bearing tokens.

cDAI is issued by [Compound Finance](https://compound.finance/) V2 on Ethereum. When users deposit DAI
into Compound V2, they receive cDAI tokens that automatically appreciate in value as interest accrues.
The exchange rate between cDAI and DAI increases continuously.

## Mechanism

- cDAI represents a share of the DAI lending pool
- Exchange rate increases over time as interest accrues (not rebasing — the balance is fixed, the rate changes)
- 8 decimal places (unlike most ERC-20 tokens)
- Can be redeemed for underlying DAI at any time

## Status

cEUR (now Mento Euro) is a Euro-pegged stablecoin native to the Celo blockchain, issued by the Mento Protocol (formerly the Celo Reserve). It is backed by a diversified on-chain reserve and designed for mobile-first payments and cross-border transactions.

cEUR was originally the Euro stablecoin of the [Celo](https://celo.org/) blockchain, issued and

- Reserve contains CELO, BTC, ETH, USDC, and other assets
- Minted and burned through Mento's on-chain exchange at oracle-determined EUR/USD rates
- Natively issued on Celo; CoinGecko now lists it as "Mento Euro"

CJPY is a Japanese Yen-pegged stablecoin issued by the Yamato Protocol on Ethereum. It is overcollateralised by ETH deposits and designed for the Japanese DeFi ecosystem. Users can mint CJPY by depositing ETH as collateral with a minimum collateral ratio of 130%.

CJPY is the native stablecoin of [Yamato Protocol](https://yamato.fi/), a CDP-based stablecoin protocol
developed for the Japanese DeFi community. It maintains a soft peg to the Japanese Yen (JPY) using
ETH as collateral.

## Mechanism

- Overcollateralised CDP model: users deposit ETH and mint CJPY
- Minimum collateral ratio: 130% (known as the "Licuefaction" threshold)
- Redemption mechanism maintains the peg by allowing CJPY holders to claim collateral
- Protocol includes a stability pool (Yamato Pledge) for absorbing liquidations

CNHT (CNH₮) is issued by [Tether](https://tether.to/), the company behind USDT, as part of its range of

crvUSD is the native stablecoin of Curve Finance, the leading decentralised exchange for stable assets. It uses the LLAMMA (Lending-Liquidating AMM Algorithm) mechanism that converts collateral to crvUSD gradually during soft liquidations, reducing liquidation risk for borrowers.

crvUSD is issued by [Curve Finance](https://curve.fi/), one of the largest and most battle-tested DEXs in DeFi.
Unlike traditional CDP stablecoins that use hard liquidations, crvUSD uses LLAMMA — an AMM-based
liquidation mechanism that gradually converts collateral to crvUSD as prices fall, allowing borrowers
more time to add collateral or repay.

## Mechanism

- Overcollateralised CDP model using various collateral types (stETH, ETH, WBTC, USDC, and others)
- LLAMMA performs soft liquidations: collateral is sold gradually across a price band rather than all at once
- Uses Curve's own price oracles (exponential moving average) for manipulation resistance
- PegKeepers maintain the peg by minting/burning crvUSD in Curve pools
- Deployed on Ethereum (primary) and bridged to multiple other chains

## Sources

- [Curve crvUSD documentation](https://resources.curve.fi/crvusd/understanding-crvusd/)

csUSD is a yield-bearing stablecoin from cSigma Finance that dynamically allocates deposits across RWA credit markets and on-chain DeFi yield strategies. It accepts multiple stablecoins as deposits via an ERC-7575 multi-asset vault. cSigma Finance connects global borrowers and lenders through tokenised real-world assets.

csUSD is issued by [cSigma Finance](https://www.csigma.finance/), a blockchain-based
protocol that tokenises private credit and connects institutional borrowers with DeFi lenders.
The stablecoin uses an ERC-7575 multi-asset vault architecture, allowing users to deposit
USDC, USDT, DAI, or other stablecoins and receive csUSD in return.

## Mechanism

csUSD dynamically allocates capital between two yield sources:
- **RWA credit markets**: Tokenised business loans to mid-market companies across the US, EU, and Asia
- **On-chain DeFi strategies**: Risk-adjusted DeFi yield strategies

The protocol autonomously rebalances between these sources based on market conditions to
optimise yield performance.

## Scale

As of Q1 2025, cSigma Finance has tokenised over $80 million in business loans,
accessible on 11 major blockchain networks including Ethereum, Arbitrum, and BNB.

[Dai](https://makerdao.com/) is a decentralised, soft-pegged stablecoin maintained by [MakerDAO](https://makerdao.com/) and the Sky protocol (formerly MakerDAO).
Users generate Dai by depositing collateral (ETH, WBTC, stablecoins, and other approved assets) into Maker Vaults and borrowing against it.
A stability fee (interest rate) accrues on all Dai positions, and positions that fall below the minimum collateralisation ratio are liquidated.

Dai has been live on Ethereum since December 2017 (initially as Single-Collateral Dai backed only by ETH, later upgraded to Multi-Collateral Dai in November 2019).
It is one of the longest-running and most battle-tested decentralised stablecoins in existence.
Holders of Dai can deposit it into the [Dai Savings Rate (DSR)](https://app.sky.money/) contract to earn yield from protocol stability fees.

MakerDAO rebranded to [Sky Protocol](https://sky.money/) in 2024, and a new stablecoin USDS was introduced as the successor to Dai, though Dai continues to circulate.

deUSD is a decentralised synthetic dollar by Elixir Protocol. It uses institutional-grade market making and delta-neutral strategies. Elixir focuses on providing deep liquidity across orderbook exchanges.

[deUSD](https://www.elixir.xyz/) is a synthetic dollar stablecoin issued by [Elixir Protocol](https://www.elixir.xyz/), a modular DeFi liquidity network focused on institutional order-book exchanges.
It maintains its peg through delta-neutral strategies that combine spot collateral with short perpetual positions, similar to the design pioneered by Ethena's USDe.

deUSD is backed by staked ETH (stETH) and other yield-bearing assets, with the yield distributed to holders of the staked version, sdeUSD.
Elixir routes liquidity to centralised and decentralised order-book venues including dYdX, Vertex, and Hyperliquid.

[Djed](https://djed.xyz/) is a formally verified, overcollateralised stablecoin protocol originally built on the [Cardano](https://cardano.org/) blockchain.
The protocol uses two tokens: DJED (the stablecoin) and SHEN (the reserve coin).
SHEN holders absorb price volatility of the collateral asset (ADA) to keep DJED pegged to USD.
The reserve ratio must remain between 400% and 800% for minting and burning to be permitted.

Djed was designed by researchers at [IOG (Input Output Global)](https://iog.io/) and deployed in collaboration with [COTI](https://coti.io/) on Cardano mainnet in January 2023.
It was one of the first major stablecoins on Cardano.
A separate DJED token also exists on EVM-compatible chains tracked by DeFiLlama.

DOLA is a decentralised stablecoin issued by Inverse Finance on Ethereum. It is backed by
various crypto collateral through the FiRM fixed-rate lending market. DOLA uses a Fed-style
monetary policy with protocol-controlled supply expansion and contraction.

[DOLA](https://www.inverse.finance/) is a decentralised USD-pegged stablecoin issued by [Inverse Finance](https://www.inverse.finance/).
It is minted through [FiRM](https://www.inverse.finance/firm), Inverse Finance's fixed-rate lending market, where users deposit collateral to borrow DOLA at a fixed interest rate.

Supply is managed via a Fed mechanism: the Inverse Finance DAO can expand or contract DOLA supply across whitelisted AMM pools and lending markets, analogous to a central bank's open market operations.
DOLA can also be staked as sDOLA to earn yield from the protocol's revenues.

Inverse Finance suffered two governance exploits in 2022 resulting in losses, but continued operating and compensating affected users over time.

text:
[DefiDollar](https://dusd.finance/) was a meta-stablecoin protocol that pooled multiple USD-pegged stablecoins (USDC, DAI, USDT, sUSD) to create a single index token with diversified stablecoin risk. By holding DUSD, users gained exposure to a basket of stablecoins without concentrating risk in any single issuer. The project was funded with $1.2 million from investors including Standard Crypto and Accomplice, and was built by the team at Yield Studio. It originated from the ETHGlobal HackMoney hackathon.

The protocol used Curve Finance LP tokens as collateral to maintain the DUSD peg. Arbitrage mechanics kept the price near $1: minting DUSD when trading above $1 and burning it when below $1. The protocol also supported a BSC deployment backed by Nerve Finance.

The DefiDollar team halted active development around 2021–2022 and pivoted to building Hubble Exchange on Solana. DUSD reached its all-time high of $1.59 in June 2021, and has traded well below its peg since the project was abandoned. The DUSD token has been marked as inactive by major data providers.

eEARN is the ERC-4626 vault-share token issued by Ember Protocol for its Earn Vault,
which accepts USDC deposits and runs opportunistic stablecoin yield strategies.
The token appreciates against USDC as the vault accumulates yield from lending spreads,
disciplined looping across blue-chip protocols, and delta-neutral funding-rate captures.

eEARN is the receipt (share) token of the [Ember Protocol](https://ember.so/) Earn Vault on
Ethereum. Ember Protocol is a unified vault platform that tokenises yield and fund strategies
across DeFi, CeFi, and Web2, incubated by Upshift Fi and Bluefin.

## Mechanism

When a user deposits USDC into the Earn Vault, they receive eEARN shares at the current
exchange rate, which starts at 1:1 and rises continuously as the vault generates yield.
The vault is managed by Ember curators who allocate pooled USDC across multiple
opportunistic stablecoin yield sources:

- **Lending-rate spreads** — supplying USDC to blue-chip money markets (Aave, Compound, etc.)
- **Disciplined looping** — leveraged lending loops to amplify stable-asset APY
- **Delta-neutral funding capture** — basis and funding-rate trades on perp DEXes

eEARN holders do not receive rebasing distributions; instead the vault's exchange rate
appreciates, meaning 1 eEARN redeems for progressively more USDC over time.

## Relationship to Royco tranches

eEARN is also the denomination token for Royco-protocol tranche vaults
(ROY-ST-eEARN / ROY-JT-eEARN) on Ethereum, which wrap eEARN shares into senior/junior
tranches that redistribute yield and risk between depositor cohorts.

[EOSDT](https://eosdt.com/) was a decentralised, overcollateralised stablecoin issued on the [EOS](https://eosnetwork.com/) blockchain by [Equilibrium](https://equilibrium.io/).
Users would lock EOS as collateral in a smart contract position to mint EOSDT at a minimum collateralisation ratio.

Equilibrium later pivoted to build a parachain on Polkadot and the EOS-based EOSDT system is no longer actively maintained.

EURA (formerly agEUR) is a Euro-pegged stablecoin issued by Angle Protocol, but it is being phased out after a February 2026 wind-down announcement. Existing holders should treat EURA as a legacy token and verify redemption options before relying on its Euro peg.

[EURA](https://www.angle.money/) (formerly known as agEUR) is a Euro-pegged stablecoin issued by [Angle Protocol](https://www.angle.money/), a decentralised stablecoin framework on Ethereum.
It was rebranded from agEUR to EURA in 2023.
The token address on Ethereum did not change with the rebrand.

Angle Protocol announced in February 2026 that EURA is being phased out through an orderly wind-down.
The token may still appear in wallets, vaults, and historical on-chain data, but it should be treated as a legacy stablecoin rather than an actively supported Euro stablecoin.
Users should verify current redemption paths and liquidity before assuming EURA trades or redeems at its Euro peg.

Angle Protocol uses a combination of mechanisms to maintain the Euro peg:
overcollateralised positions (similar to Maker Vaults), yield-bearing reserves, and algorithmic rebalancing across supported chains.
EURA can be bridged across multiple EVM networks via the LayerZero-based Angle bridge.

EUR CoinVertible (EURCV) is a Euro-denominated security token issued by SG-FORGE, a subsidiary of Societe Generale. It is a regulated digital asset backed by Euro reserves for institutional use. EURCV bridges traditional finance and DeFi.

[EUR CoinVertible (EURCV)](https://www.sgforge.com/product/coinvertible/) is a Euro-denominated stablecoin issued by [SG-FORGE](https://www.sgforge.com/), the digital asset subsidiary of French bank Société Générale.
It was the first institutional stablecoin deployed on a public blockchain by a major European bank, launched in April 2023 on Ethereum.

EURCV is a regulated instrument designed for institutional participants.
It is fully backed by Euros held in reserve and settles on-chain, enabling DeFi integrations while complying with applicable securities regulations.
SG-FORGE has subsequently deployed EURCV in DeFi protocols including MakerDAO (now Sky) and Aave.
In 2025, SG-FORGE expanded EURCV to the Stellar blockchain and also announced a USD-denominated stablecoin (USDCV) with BNY as custodian.

EURe is a Euro-backed electronic money token issued by Monerium, a licensed e-money institution in Europe. Each EURe is fully backed by Euros held in European bank accounts. It is available on Ethereum, Polygon, and Gnosis Chain.

[EURe](https://monerium.com/) is an electronic money token (EMT) issued by [Monerium](https://monerium.com/), an Icelandic company licensed as an electronic money institution (EMI) under EU regulation.
Each EURe is fully backed 1:1 by Euro deposits held in segregated European bank accounts.

Users can send Euros from their bank account to a Monerium IBAN and receive EURe on-chain, or burn EURe to receive Euros back in their bank account.

[fxUSD](https://fx.aladdin.club/) is a USD-pegged stablecoin issued by the
[f(x) Protocol](https://docs.aladdin.club/f-x-protocol), a DeFi primitive built by
[Aladdin DAO](https://aladdin.club/) on Ethereum. Unlike conventional stablecoins, fxUSD

fluctuations of the underlying collateral. This invariant ensures fxUSD remains 100%

fees, and FXN token emissions is distributed to liquidity providers.

- Backed by stETH and wBTC; no fiat or centralised custodians
- 100% collateralisation maintained by the f(x) invariant
- Yield distributed via the fxSAVE module for flexible savings

gDAI represents DAI deposited into the Gains Network (gTrade) vault on Arbitrum and Polygon. It earns yield from trading fees generated by the gTrade decentralised leverage trading platform. gDAI acts as the counterparty to traders on the platform.

[Gains Network](https://gains.trade/) operates [gTrade](https://gains.trade/), a decentralised
leveraged trading platform on Arbitrum (and previously Polygon). gDAI is the ERC-4626-compliant
vault token representing DAI deposited into the platform's liquidity vault.

## Mechanism

The gDAI vault acts as the direct counterparty to all trades on gTrade:

- When traders close winning positions, their profits are paid out of the vault
- When traders close losing positions, those losses flow into the vault
- In exchange, the vault receives a share of all trading fees generated by the platform
- If collateralisation falls below a threshold, the GNS token serves as a backstop

## Epoch system

Because computing open profit/loss on-chain in real time is too expensive, the vault uses an
epoch system. During each epoch, a network of oracles submits open PnL snapshots; the median
is taken and averaged across request periods. Withdrawals are processed during designated
withdrawal windows within each epoch.

## Key properties

- ERC-4626 tokenised vault — gDAI shares are freely transferable and composable
- Yield is variable: positive when traders net-lose, negative when traders net-win
- No fixed APY; returns depend entirely on trader PnL on the platform

gmdUSDC is a receipt token issued by [GMD Protocol](https://gmdprotocol.com/), a yield aggregation
protocol on Arbitrum. When a user deposits USDC into GMD's single-sided vault, they receive gmdUSDC
representing their share of the position. The token auto-compounds, appreciating continuously in
value at the vault's current APY rate — holders do not need to manually claim rewards.

## Mechanism

GMD Protocol is built on top of [GMX](https://gmx.io/) and its GLP liquidity provider token.
The protocol maintains a pseudo-delta-neutral strategy: GMD's BTC, ETH, and USDC vaults hold
assets in proportions mirroring GLP's composition, which is periodically rebalanced. This structure
allows stablecoin depositors to capture GLP trading fee revenue while maintaining delta-neutral
exposure — they earn a share of traders' losses and fees without direct price exposure to ETH/BTC.

A protocol reserve offsets impermanent losses arising from GLP's asset-composition imbalances.
The USDC vault historically offered APYs ranging from 7% to 30%+ depending on GLP trading volumes.

gmdUSDC holders can additionally provide liquidity in Uniswap v3 paired with raw USDC, earning
extra trading fees with minimal impermanent loss whilst retaining vault yield.

## Key properties

- Single-sided USDC deposit; no directional crypto exposure
- Yield sourced from GMX GLP trading fees and traders' losses
- Auto-compounding receipt token (value appreciates, no manual claims)
- Deployed on Arbitrum

gmUSD is a stablecoin from the GND Protocol designed around GMX's GLP and GM tokens. It uses delta-neutral strategies on GMX positions. gmUSD is available on Arbitrum.

[GND Protocol](https://gndprotocol.com/) is a DeFi protocol on Arbitrum that issues gmUSD, a yield-bearing stablecoin backed by delta-neutral positions on GMX and Gains Network. The protocol combines the GLP/GM ecosystem of GMX with yield-bearing collateral from GMD Protocol and Gains Network to produce a stablecoin that earns real yield for its holders.

gmUSD is fully collateralised by two underlying assets: gmdUSDC (the USDC vault within GMD Protocol, which acts as a delta-neutral counterpart to GLP on GMX) and gDAI (a delta-neutral liquidity provider token on Gains Network that earns protocol fees by acting as a counterparty to perpetual trades). Because both collateral assets generate real yield from trading fees, gmUSD itself is yield-bearing at an expected annualised rate of approximately 15–25%.

## Peg mechanism

The peg is maintained via a Protocol Smart Arbitrage Leverage Mechanism (PSALM). GND Protocol is the sole entity authorised to mint and redeem gmUSD, using gDAI and gmdUSDC as collateral at a $1 reference price. If gmUSD trades above $1, the protocol mints new tokens at $1 and sells them to capture the premium; if it trades below $1, the protocol buys and redeems them. This closed arbitrage loop ensures the protocol itself always captures the arbitrage profit before any third party can.

Gyroscope Dollar (GYD) is a decentralised stablecoin designed with an all-weather reserve structure. It uses concentrated liquidity pools and a novel redemption mechanism to maintain its peg. GYD aims to be resilient against black swan events through diversified backing.

[Gyroscope Dollar (GYD)](https://www.gyro.finance/) is a fully-backed decentralised stablecoin issued by
the Gyroscope protocol. It targets a 1 USD peg and is designed to be resilient against the systemic
risks that have caused other stablecoins to fail, including oracle failures, governance attacks, and
collateral contagion.

## Mechanism

GYD is backed by an "all-weather" reserve — a diversified portfolio of DeFi assets spread across
segregated vaults, each representing a distinct risk dimension (censorship, regulatory, counterparty,
oracle, and governance risk). If one vault is compromised, the failure is contained and does not
cascade through the system.

Minting and redemption are governed by autonomous pricing curves with dynamic fees and circuit
breakers. When GYD trades above $1, users can mint at a slight premium; when it trades below, they
can redeem from the reserve. This arbitrage mechanism keeps the peg tightly anchored.

GYD liquidity is concentrated in Elliptic Concentrated Liquidity Pools (E-CLPs), a novel AMM
primitive developed by Gyroscope and built on [Balancer](https://balancer.fi/). E-CLPs concentrate
liquidity asymmetrically along an elliptical curve around the peg price, improving capital
efficiency relative to constant-product or StableSwap designs.

## Key properties

- Fully backed by a diversified, vault-segregated all-weather reserve
- E-CLP AMM provides deep, capital-efficient peg liquidity on Balancer
- sGYD: a yield-bearing ERC-4626 wrapper where deposited GYD earns reserve yield
- GYFI governance token used for protocol parameter control and revenue distribution
- Deployed on Ethereum mainnet (December 2023) and Arbitrum

Iron was a partially algorithmic stablecoin by Iron Finance on Polygon. It suffered a bank-run-style collapse in June 2021 when its TITAN collateral token lost nearly all value. The project is now defunct and serves as a cautionary example of algorithmic stablecoin design.

[Iron Finance](https://iron.finance/) issued IRON as a partially algorithmic stablecoin on the
Polygon network. IRON was backed by a combination of 75% USDC and 25% TITAN (Iron Finance's
native governance token), with the Target Collateral Ratio (TCR) determining the exact split
at any given time.

## Mechanism

To mint $1 of IRON, users deposited USDC and TITAN in the required ratio. The TITAN portion
was burned on mint and newly minted on redemption, creating reflexive supply dynamics. A 10-minute
TWAP oracle was used to price TITAN for redemption purposes.

## Collapse (June 2021)

On 16 June 2021, large holders began removing liquidity from the IRON/USDC pool and selling TITAN,
causing IRON to depeg. Because the TWAP oracle lagged the spot price, redemptions minted more TITAN
than the spot price implied, flooding the market with new TITAN supply. This triggered a
hyperinflationary death spiral — TITAN fell from ~$65 to effectively $0 within hours, taking IRON
well below its $1 peg. The event is widely cited as crypto's first large-scale DeFi bank run,
with estimated losses of approximately $2 billion. Notable investors including Mark Cuban were
affected.

Iron Finance published a post-mortem on 17 June 2021 attributing the collapse to design flaws in
the arbitrage mechanism and oracle latency. The project is now defunct.

iUSD is a synthetic USD stablecoin on the Cardano blockchain issued by Indigo Protocol. It is overcollateralised by ADA and uses a CDP model inspired by MakerDAO. iUSD is the primary decentralised stablecoin in the Cardano DeFi ecosystem.

iUSD is the primary decentralised stablecoin on the [Cardano](https://cardano.org/) blockchain,
issued by [Indigo Protocol](https://indigoprotocol.io/) — a Cardano-native CDP (Collateralised
Debt Position) protocol. Launched in November 2022, iUSD was Cardano's first fault-tolerant and
fully collateralised native stablecoin.

## Mechanism

Users mint iUSD by depositing ADA as collateral into a CDP, subject to a Minimum Collateralisation
Ratio (MCR). The protocol requires overcollateralisation to ensure solvency. If the ADA collateral
value falls towards the MCR threshold, the Indigo Stability Pool provides automatic liquidation:
Stability Pool iUSD is exchanged for the higher-value ADA collateral, keeping iUSD fully backed
at all times.

Rather than pegging iUSD directly to any single fiat-backed stablecoin, the peg target is the
median value of USDC, TUSD, and USDT — a fault-tolerant design that maintains stability even if
one of the reference stablecoins depegs.

A notable innovation is CDP Liquid Staking: ADA deposited as collateral continues to earn native
Cardano staking rewards throughout the life of the CDP, improving capital efficiency for borrowers.

## Key properties

- Overcollateralised by ADA; Cardano-native
- Peg anchored to the median of USDC, TUSD, and USDT
- Stability Pool backstop prevents undercollateralisation
- CDP Liquid Staking: collateral ADA still earns staking rewards
- Governed by INDY token holders

iUSD is a yield-bearing stablecoin issued by infiniFi on Ethereum. It is pegged to the US dollar and earns yield for holders through the infiniFi protocol's liquidity management strategies. iUSD has approximately $170M in circulating supply as of early 2026.

[infiniFi](https://app.infinifi.org/) is an Ethereum-based DeFi protocol that replicates the structure of fractional reserve banking on-chain. Users deposit USDC to receive iUSD, a 1:1 USD-pegged receipt stablecoin. The protocol then deploys those reserves into yield strategies — principally money-market protocols such as Aave and Fluid, as well as Pendle fixed-income markets — and distributes the resulting yield back to token holders.

iUSD holders can choose between two yield-bearing derivatives with different liquidity and risk profiles. Staking iUSD produces siUSD (liquid, lower yield), while locking iUSD produces liUSD (illiquid for a fixed term, higher yield). Capital in the siUSD tranche is deployed conservatively into low-risk money markets, while the liUSD tranche can access higher-risk, higher-return strategies. In the event of a loss, liUSD holders absorb losses first, then siUSD stakers, before plain iUSD holders are affected.

## Reserve transparency

All reserve deployments are visible on-chain, giving users full visibility into the asset–liability composition of the protocol at any time, without relying on quarterly attestations. infiniFi had approximately $170M in circulating iUSD as of early 2026.

- Native Tezos (FA2 token standard), not EVM-based
- Purely algorithmic and over-collateralised — no fiat backing
- Soft-pegged to USD via XTZ collateral and arbitrage incentives

mtUSDC represents USDC deposited in the Mutuum Finance lending protocol. It is a yield-bearing receipt token that accrues interest from borrowers. Mutuum Finance provides decentralised lending and borrowing on Ethereum.

[mtUSDC](https://docs.mutuum.com/introduction/concepts/mttokens) is a yield-bearing receipt token issued by [Mutuum Finance](https://www.mutuum.com/), an Ethereum-based decentralised, non-custodial lending and borrowing protocol. When a user deposits USDC into a Mutuum liquidity pool, they receive an equivalent amount of mtUSDC representing their share of the pool and the interest it accumulates.

## Mechanism

mtUSDC accrues value continuously as borrowers repay loans with interest. Rather than distributing additional tokens, each mtUSDC becomes redeemable for a growing amount of the underlying USDC over time. When a user redeems, they return mtUSDC to Mutuum's contracts and receive their original USDC principal plus all accrued interest, subject to available pool liquidity. Because mtUSDC is a standard ERC-20 token, it is transferable and can be integrated with other DeFi protocols.

## Key properties

- Fully ERC-20 compliant and transferable
- Value accrues automatically — no manual claiming or compounding required
- Backed by USDC deposited in Mutuum's peer-to-contract lending pools
- Mutuum Finance raised over $20 million in its pre-launch phase (as of March 2026)
- V1 Protocol launched on Sepolia testnet prior to Ethereum mainnet deployment

mtUSDT represents USDT deposited in the Mutuum Finance lending protocol. It is a yield-bearing receipt token that accrues interest from borrowers. Mutuum Finance provides decentralised lending and borrowing on Ethereum.

[mtUSDT](https://www.mutuum.com/) is a yield-bearing receipt token issued by
[Mutuum Finance](https://www.mutuum.com/), a decentralised, non-custodial liquidity protocol on
Ethereum. When a lender deposits USDT into the Mutuum Finance lending pool, they receive an
equivalent amount of mtUSDT that automatically accrues interest over time as borrowers pay back
loans with interest.

## Mechanism

Mutuum Finance uses a Peer-to-Contract (P2C) model: lenders deposit assets such as USDT or ETH
into shared liquidity reserves, and borrowers draw from these pools by providing over-collateralised
assets. The interest rate adjusts dynamically based on pool utilisation. mtUSDT tokens serve as
1:1 proof of deposit and appreciate in value relative to USDT as the pool earns interest — similar
to Aave's aToken model.

The protocol's V1 was deployed to the Sepolia testnet in early 2026 after a fundraising round that
exceeded $20 million from over 19,000 participants. Mainnet launch was targeted to follow the
testnet phase. A planned Phase 2 also includes a native over-collateralised stablecoin backed by
on-chain collateral.

## Key properties

- 1:1 receipt token: 1 mtUSDT = 1 USDT deposited, appreciating as interest accrues
- Yield sourced from over-collateralised borrowers on the same pool
- Non-custodial: users retain control; the smart contract holds reserves
- Initial supported assets: USDT and ETH

satUSD is an overcollateralised stablecoin issued by [Satoshi Protocol](https://www.satoshiprotocol.org/)
(now operating under the [River](https://river.inc/) brand). It is the first Bitcoin Finance (BTCFi)
stablecoin built around an Omni-CDP model, enabling users to collateralise BTC-denominated assets on
one chain and mint satUSD natively on another — without wrapping or bridging.

## Mechanism

Users deposit collateral — including BTCB, wBTC, tBTC, solvBTC, ETH, BNB, and various liquid staking
tokens — and mint satUSD subject to a minimum collateralisation ratio of 110–150% depending on the
asset. A one-time minting fee applies (0.5%–5%). Cross-chain minting is powered by
[LayerZero's OFT standard](https://layerzero.network/), allowing satUSD to circulate across EVM
networks and Solana without a traditional bridge.

The peg is maintained through real-time liquidations, on-chain arbitrage, and five layers of risk
control. Users can stake satUSD to receive satUSD+, a yield-bearing token that shares protocol revenue.

With the rebrand to River, the protocol expanded its chain-abstraction approach: users can collateralise
assets on Ethereum, Base, BSC, Hemi, or BOB, and mint satUSD on any supported destination chain.

## Key properties

- BTC-native and EVM multi-chain; powered by LayerZero OFT
- Overcollateralised CDP; minimum ratio 110–150% depending on asset
- Integrated with Chainlink Price Feeds for oracle security
- Yield-bearing satUSD+ staking token

chain-abstraction system. River evolved from Satoshi Protocol v2 into a full chain-abstraction
stablecoin infrastructure, with satUSD as its core liquidity primitive.

## Mechanism

River's Omni-CDP model allows users to collateralise assets on a source chain and mint satUSD
natively on any destination chain supported by LayerZero OFT — no bridges or wrapped assets are
required. Supported collateral includes BTC, ETH, BNB, and various liquid staking tokens (LSTs).
satUSD supply was approximately $293 million as of September 2025, deployed across Hemi, BSC,
Ethereum, Base, and BOB.

Users can stake satUSD to receive satUSD+, a yield-bearing token that accrues protocol revenue.
River also offers a Prime Vault product for institutional depositors, integrated with leading
custodians for operational simplicity.

sUSD3 is the **junior tranche** of the [3Jane](https://www.3jane.xyz/) credit
protocol, obtained by staking USD3 (the senior tranche). It is an ERC-4626 token whose
underlying asset is USD3 rather than USDC directly, so its value is denominated through
USD3's USDC peg.

## Mechanism

Junior depositors stake USD3 to mint sUSD3 and, in return for accepting first-loss risk,
receive a higher proportion of the lending pool's yield. sUSD3 absorbs losses before USD3
is impaired in the loss waterfall, and junior positions are subject to a one-month lock.
Like USD3, sUSD3 appreciates against its underlying as interest accrues — yield is
reflected in the exchange rate rather than rebasing distributions, and additional $JANE
emissions can layer on top.

## Relationship to USD3

dollar-denominated stablecoin on the chain and underpinned the majority of early Base DeFi

lock-and-mint model: USDC is locked in an Ethereum smart contract and an equivalent amount

releases the original USDC on Ethereum. Because it is a bridged representation rather than

Circle launched natively issued USDC on Base in September 2023. Native USDC is minted
directly by Circle on Base and is fully redeemable 1:1 for US dollars through Circle's
standard redemption channels. The Base ecosystem has since encouraged a gradual migration
of liquidity from USDbC to native USDC. Both tokens continue to coexist on-chain, but
native USDC has become the canonical stablecoin for new integrations, and USDbC is
considered a legacy asset.

USDC.e (also written as USDCe or "bridged USDC") is a form of USDC that has been transferred from Ethereum to another blockchain via a canonical bridge. When USDC is bridged, the original tokens are locked in a smart contract on Ethereum and an equivalent amount of USDC.e is minted on the destination chain. The ".e" suffix indicates the token's Ethereum origin. USDC.e is **not** issued directly by [Circle](https://www.circle.com/usdc); rather it is a wrapped representation of Circle-issued USDC.

## Mechanism

Bridging works by locking USDC on Ethereum and minting a corresponding USDC.e token on the destination network (e.g. Arbitrum One, Avalanche C-Chain, Polygon PoS, Optimism). The bridge operator is typically the canonical bridge for that network. Redemption reverses the process: burning USDC.e on the destination chain releases the locked USDC on Ethereum.

## Migration to native USDC

As Circle began deploying native USDC directly on Layer-2 networks in mid-2023 (Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon, Base, and others via the Cross-Chain Transfer Protocol, CCTP), USDC.e began to be phased out on chains where native USDC exists. [USD Coin (USDC)](https://www.circle.com/usdc) is a fully-reserved, fiat-backed stablecoin issued
by [Circle](https://www.circle.com/). Each USDC token is backed 1:1 by cash and short-dated US
government obligations held at regulated US financial institutions. Circle publishes monthly
attestation reports from independent accountants confirming that reserves always equal or exceed
the outstanding USDC supply. USDC is one of the two largest stablecoins by market capitalisation
and a cornerstone of on-chain liquidity across DeFi and CeFi.

## Issuance and reserves

USDC was originally launched in 2018 as a joint venture between Circle and Coinbase under the
Centre Consortium; Circle became the sole issuer after acquiring the Centre infrastructure in 2023.
Reserves are held in segregated accounts at US banks and in the BlackRock USD Institutional Digital
Liquidity Fund (BUIDL), providing transparency and liquidity. USDC can be minted or redeemed
directly by verified institutional and business accounts at a 1:1 rate.

## Cross-chain and native issuance

Unlike bridged representations, Circle issues USDC natively on more than 20 blockchains, including
Ethereum, Solana, Arbitrum, Base, Avalanche, Polygon, and others. Cross-chain transfers use
Circle's Cross-Chain Transfer Protocol (CCTP), which burns USDC on the source chain and mints
fresh native USDC on the destination chain, preserving fungibility and eliminating bridge custodial
risk.

## Regulatory standing

Circle holds money transmitter licences in 47 US states and Electronic Money Institution (EMI)
status in several European jurisdictions. In 2025 the US Congress passed the GENIUS Act, which
established a federal framework for payment stablecoin issuers; USDC's reserve structure was
already substantively aligned with those requirements. The SEC confirmed in 2025 that "Covered
Stablecoins" such as USDC do not constitute securities.

## Key properties

- Fully reserved: cash and short-dated US Treasuries, attested monthly
- Natively issued on 20+ blockchains; cross-chain transfers via CCTP (burn-and-mint)
- Regulated US issuer with state money transmitter licences and European EMI status
- Widely integrated in DeFi protocols (Aave, Compound, Uniswap, Curve, etc.) and CeFi exchanges

SG-FORGE also issues EUR CoinVertible (EURCV), the EUR-denominated counterpart, which was

USDD is a decentralised stablecoin on the TRON network backed by the TRON DAO Reserve. It is overcollateralised by TRX, BTC, USDT, and other assets. USDD uses a hybrid algorithmic and reserve-backed mechanism.

[USDD](https://usdd.io/) (Decentralised USD) is a stablecoin issued by the
[TRON DAO Reserve](https://tdr.org/) and launched in April 2022 by TRON founder
Justin Sun. It was initially designed as an algorithmic stablecoin inspired by
Terra's UST, but was restructured into a fully overcollateralised model following the
Terra/LUNA collapse in May 2022. The "USDD 2.0" upgrade in January 2025 formalised
this overcollateralised structure.

## Mechanism

USDD maintains its peg through a combination of over-collateralisation and a TRX
mint-and-burn mechanism. The TRON DAO Reserve holds a basket of assets — including TRX,
BTC, USDT, and USDC — with a minimum collateral ratio of 130%. When USDD trades below
$1, arbitrageurs can burn USDD to mint TRX at a profit; when USDD trades above $1, TRX
can be burned to mint USDD. The reserve is publicly verifiable on-chain. USDD launched
natively on Ethereum in September 2025 and on BNB Chain in October 2025.

## Key properties

- Overcollateralised by a diversified reserve (TRX, BTC, USDC, USDT)
- Minimum 130% collateral ratio maintained by TRON DAO Reserve
- TRX mint-and-burn arbitrage mechanism for peg maintenance
- Available on TRON, Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain, and Arbitrum
- CertiK AA security rating (November 2025)

## Status

As of early 2026, USDD has approximately $750 million in circulating supply. Despite
multiple brief depegging events in 2022 and 2023, it has largely maintained its $1 peg
under the overcollateralised model.

USDe is a synthetic dollar protocol by Ethena Labs that uses delta-hedging staked ETH positions. It generates yield through staking rewards and futures funding rates. USDe is one of the fastest-growing stablecoins by market capitalisation.

[Ethena](https://ethena.fi/) is a synthetic dollar protocol on Ethereum. USDe achieves its
dollar peg through a delta-neutral strategy rather than fiat reserves or overcollateralisation.

## Mechanism

Users or whitelisted minting partners deposit collateral (ETH, stETH, BTC, USDT, or USDC).
Ethena simultaneously opens an equivalent-sized short perpetual futures position on centralised
derivatives exchanges. Because the short exactly offsets the long collateral exposure, the
combined position is delta-neutral — its USD value is stable regardless of asset price movements.

Yield is generated from two sources:

1. **Staking rewards** — stETH (and other liquid staking tokens) earn Ethereum consensus and
   execution layer rewards
2. **Funding rates** — perpetual futures traders who are long typically pay a positive funding
   rate to short-holders; Ethena captures this as revenue

The yield-bearing version, [sUSDe](https://ethena.fi/susde), auto-compounds these returns for
stakers. Ethena describes sUSDe as the "Internet Bond".

## Key properties

- No fiat bank accounts — fully on-chain and crypto-native collateral
- Custodied off-exchange via institutional OES (off-exchange settlement) providers
- Negative funding rate risk: if perpetual funding turns persistently negative, the protocol
  draws from an insurance fund to maintain the peg
- One of the fastest-growing stablecoins by market cap, reaching $6B+ in 2024

[Falcon Finance](https://falcon.finance/) issues USDf as a synthetic dollar backed by
hedged crypto positions. Users deposit eligible assets — stablecoins such as USDC/USDT
at a 1:1 ratio, or non-stablecoin crypto assets — which are overcollateralised and
delta-hedged by Falcon's proprietary trading strategies. The protocol targets institutional
and DeFi participants seeking stable yield.

## Mechanism

Falcon maintains the USD peg through a delta-neutral strategy: spot crypto positions are
offset by short perpetual futures positions, eliminating directional price exposure. The
protocol captures yield from positive funding rates (holding spot, shorting perps) and
can also generate returns in negative funding rate environments by inverting the position.
An on-chain Insurance Fund provides a backstop against extreme market stress.

Reserve attestations are published weekly by HT Digital, with quarterly ISAE 3000
assurance reports, providing verifiable proof of backing.

sUSDf is the staked, yield-bearing version of USDf: holders deposit USDf to receive sUSDf,

USDf is an overcollateralised synthetic dollar issued by [Falcon Finance](https://falcon.finance/),
a Universal Collateral Infrastructure protocol designed for both institutional and DeFi users.
USDf is minted by depositing collateral assets and is maintained at a $1 peg through a combination
of delta-neutral and market-neutral strategies.

## Mechanism

Stablecoin deposits mint USDf at a 1:1 ratio. Non-stablecoin and real-world asset (RWA) deposits
use a dynamic Overcollateralisation Ratio (OCR) calibrated to the asset's volatility, liquidity,
and historical behaviour — ensuring the total collateral value always exceeds USDf in circulation.

Deposited collateral is actively managed to achieve delta neutrality: Falcon neutralises directional
price exposure by holding spot assets while shorting perpetual futures (funding-rate arbitrage), or
by selling spot and going long futures in negative-rate environments. This means USDf holders are
insulated from collateral price movements.

Yield is distributed to holders who stake USDf into sUSDf, a yield-bearing token that compounds
returns from the delta-neutral strategies and RWA income. Falcon also maintains a $10 million
insurance fund and audits its segregated reserves weekly.

- Overcollateralised synthetic dollar; dynamic OCR for volatile assets
- Delta-neutral collateral management via funding-rate arbitrage
- sUSDf: yield-bearing staking token backed by protocol strategies

- Institutional focus with DeFi accessibility

The USDF Consortium is a network of FDIC-insured banks creating a bank-minted stablecoin. USDF is designed for interbank settlement and compliant digital transactions. The consortium includes multiple US banking institutions.

The [USDF Consortium](https://usdfconsortium.com/) is an association of FDIC-insured US financial
institutions that launched in January 2022 with the goal of developing and promoting a bank-minted
tokenised deposit stablecoin. Unlike privately issued stablecoins, USDF is minted exclusively by
regulated member banks and is redeemable 1:1 for cash from any Consortium member bank.

## Mechanism

USDF operates on a permissioned blockchain based on the [Provenance Blockchain](https://provenance.io/)
codebase. Although the Consortium initially used the public Provenance chain, it subsequently migrated
to a private, permissioned fork ("USDF Private Chain") following regulatory feedback from US bank
supervisors that participation in public, permissionless chains posed elevated risk.

Each member bank mints USDF directly when a customer wishes to transact on-chain; the corresponding
cash is held as a deposit at that bank. Redemptions are honoured at par by any Consortium member.
Use cases under development include interbank settlement, loan securitisation, and cross-border payments.

## Status

As of early 2024, the technology infrastructure was built and members were awaiting full regulatory
approval before going live at scale. The Consortium had grown to nine bank members, including New York
Community Bank, FirstBank, NBH Bank, Synovus, Webster Bank, ConnectOne Bank, Amerant Bank, Primis Bank,
and Atlantic Union Bank.

## Key properties

- Bank-minted tokenised deposit; only FDIC-insured banks may issue
- Redeemable 1:1 for cash at any member bank
- Private permissioned Provenance-based blockchain
- Regulatory compliance focus; no public issuance

[Global Dollar (USDG)](https://globaldollar.com/) is a USD-backed stablecoin issued by
Paxos Digital Singapore Pte. Ltd. and governed under the
[Global Dollar Network](https://globaldollar.com/) — a consortium of major financial and
crypto firms including Anchorage Digital, Bullish, Galaxy Digital, Kraken, Nuvei, Paxos,
and Robinhood. Mastercard and Fiserv subsequently joined the network. USDG launched in
November 2024 and is substantively compliant with the Monetary Authority of Singapore
(MAS) stablecoin framework; it is also issued in Europe by Paxos Issuance Europe under
MiCA supervision by the Finnish Financial Supervisory Authority (FIN-FSA).

## Reserve backing

Every USDG token is backed 1:1 by high-quality liquid assets: US dollar deposits, short-
duration US government securities, and equivalent cash instruments. Reserves are held and
managed by Paxos Digital Singapore via DBS Bank, with monthly third-party attestation
reports published publicly.

## Yield-sharing model

The defining feature of USDG is its revenue-sharing design. Approximately 97% of the net
interest income generated by the reserve assets is distributed back to Global Dollar Network
partners in proportion to their contribution to USDG adoption and liquidity. Partners can
earn yield on USDG balances held on their platforms and receive additional revenue for
minting and accepting the token — an incentive structure intended to accelerate stablecoin
adoption across exchanges, wallets, and payment networks.

## Technical details

USDG is an ERC-20 token on Ethereum (contract `0xe343167631d89B6Ffc58B88d6b7fB0228795491D`)
and is also available on Arbitrum, Ink, Robinhood Chain, Solana, and X Layer. Paxos publishes
the canonical USDG token addresses in its developer documentation, including the Robinhood
Chain deployment at `0x5fc5360D0400a0Fd4f2af552ADD042D716F1d168`.

Robinhood Chain support was announced by Global Dollar Network on 1 July 2026. The announcement
describes USDG as the first stablecoin natively issued on Robinhood Chain and the default lending
asset for Robinhood's onchain self-custodial Earn product.

The Ethereum contract uses OpenZeppelin's UUPS upgradeable proxy pattern. Source code is published
at [github.com/paxosglobal/usdg-contract](https://github.com/paxosglobal/usdg-contract).

[USDH](https://nativemarkets.xyz/) is the native stablecoin of the
[Hyperliquid](https://hyperliquid.xyz/) L1 blockchain, issued by
[Native Markets](https://nativemarkets.xyz/). The issuer was selected through a competitive

It is the world's first regulated yield-bearing stablecoin pegged 1:1 to the US dollar and fully collateralised by tokenised US Treasury Bills.

text:
USDT.e is a bridged representation of [Tether (USDT)](https://tether.to/) on L2 and alt-L1
blockchains where Tether has not yet deployed a natively minted contract. The ".e" suffix
(sometimes also written as "USDT.e" or displayed as "Bridged USDT") indicates the token was
brought to the target chain via that chain's canonical bridge.

## Mechanism

The bridging process works as follows:

1. USDT on Ethereum is locked in the canonical bridge smart contract
2. An equivalent amount of USDT.e is minted on the destination chain by the bridge
3. To exit, the user burns USDT.e and the bridge releases the locked USDT on Ethereum

This means USDT.e is always backed 1:1 by real USDT held in the bridge contract — it inherits
both Tether's USD reserves backing and the security model of the canonical bridge.

## Deployment context

USDT.e has appeared on several chains including Avalanche (via Avalanche Bridge),
Arbitrum (via Arbitrum Bridge before native USDT launched), Optimism, and others. As Tether
expands its native deployments, USDT.e versions are gradually superseded by native USDT,
and liquidity migrates over time.

## Key properties

- Backed 1:1 by USDT locked on Ethereum in the canonical bridge
- Bridge risk: the security of USDT.e depends on the bridge contract in addition to Tether's reserves
- Being phased out on chains where Tether now issues native USDT directly

- [Tether official site](https://tether.to/)
- [Avalanche Bridge documentation](https://core.app/help/bridge)

A new Terra blockchain was launched, without UST. The collapse triggered global regulatory scrutiny of algorithmic stablecoins.

wind down its operations. TFL shut down its products on October 30, 2024, with the terra.money
homepage now displaying a formal wind-down notice. The Terra blockchain was transitioned to
community management.

## Mechanism

Because xDAI is the native coin of Gnosis Chain (analogous to ETH on Ethereum), it does not

xDAI to be used seamlessly within DeFi protocols, decentralised exchanges, and liquidity pools
that require standard ERC-20 tokens.

The wrapping contract is a standard WETH-style contract deployed on Gnosis Chain at

unwrapping burns WXDAI and returns xDAI.

Tether Gold (XAU₮, ticker XAUT) is a gold-backed digital token issued by
[TG Commodities Limited](https://gold.tether.to/), a company associated with Tether. Each XAUT token
represents ownership of one fine troy ounce of physical gold stored in a dedicated Swiss vault,
allowing investors to hold tokenised gold on-chain without a traditional custodian intermediary.

## Mechanism

Each XAUT token is linked to a specific, individually numbered LBMA-certified (London Good Delivery)
gold bar held in a Swiss vault controlled by TG Commodities Limited. New XAUT tokens are minted when
physical gold enters storage, and tokens are burned when gold exits through redemption — maintaining
the strict 1:1 backing ratio. Holders can verify their allocation against numbered gold bars.

Full physical redemption is available to holders owning at least one LBMA Good Delivery bar
(approximately 430 troy ounces), with delivery arranged directly from the Swiss vaults. Smaller
holders can redeem for cash.

## Transparency and audits

TG Commodities Limited publishes quarterly limited-assurance attestation reports audited by
[BDO Italia](https://www.bdo.it/), verifying 1:1 backing, physical existence, gold bar allocation,
and insurance coverage. As of Q1 2025, more than 7.7 tonnes of physical gold backed XAUT tokens
in circulation. Tether also integrates [Chainlink Proof of Reserve](https://chain.link/proof-of-reserve)
oracles for real-time on-chain reserve verification.

## Key properties

- 1 XAUT = 1 fine troy ounce of LBMA Good Delivery gold
- Physical gold stored in Swiss vaults; no fractional reserve
- Quarterly BDO attestations; Chainlink PoR on-chain verification
- Available on Ethereum and Tron
- No management fees charged by TG Commodities

xDAI is the native gas token of [Gnosis Chain](https://www.gnosis.io/) (formerly xDai Chain), a proof-of-stake EVM-compatible sidechain. It is pegged 1:1 to DAI and is used to pay all transaction fees on Gnosis Chain, making it one of the earliest live examples of a blockchain that uses a stablecoin — rather than a volatile asset — as its native currency.

The xDai Chain was launched in October 2018 by POA Network. The chain was originally called xDai Chain and was built by POA Network. It adopted proof-of-stake validator consensus (POSDAO) in April 2020. In December 2021 the chain merged with Gnosis and was rebranded to Gnosis Chain, with the STAKE governance token replaced by GNO. xDAI itself retained its name and 1:1 DAI peg and remains the native gas token of Gnosis Chain.

[Zephyr Protocol](https://www.zephyrprotocol.com/) is an independent privacy-focused blockchain
forked from Monero. It implements the academically peer-reviewed
[Djed](https://iohk.io/en/research/library/papers/djed-a-formally-verified-crypto-backed-pegged-algorithmic-stablecoin/)
stablecoin algorithm on top of Monero's privacy primitives, yielding a fully untraceable
stablecoin system.

## Mechanism

Zephyr Protocol has three native assets:

- **ZEPH** — the base reserve coin (mined via proof-of-work)
- **ZSD (Zephyr Stable Dollar)** — the USD-pegged stablecoin
- **ZRS (Zephyr Reserve Share)** — reserve shares that absorb collateral volatility

Users mint ZSD by depositing ZEPH into the protocol's reserve at oracle-reported prices.
ZSD requires a minimum 400% collateralisation ratio (i.e. $4 of ZEPH backs every $1 of ZSD),
substantially above comparable CDP systems. ZRS holders earn from reserve appreciation when
ZEPH rises, and absorb losses when it falls, protecting ZSD's peg.

## Privacy properties

Because Zephyr inherits Monero's RingCT and stealth address technology, all transactions —
including ZSD transfers — are confidential and untraceable by default. This distinguishes ZSD
from every other stablecoin: the sender, receiver, and amount are all hidden on-chain.

and community governance. Twitter activity was last observed in August 2025.

Counterparty liquidity vault for dominance perpetual futures on Base.

Domination Finance is a perpetual futures exchange for dominance indices:
the relative market share of major crypto assets such as BTCDOM, ETHDOM,
USDTDOM, BNBDOM and SOLDOM. Traders can use leverage on these proprietary
oracle-backed markets.

The dfUSDC vault is the protocol's liquidity backbone. It is an ERC-4626
vault on Base where users deposit native USDC and receive dfUSDC shares.
Vault capital acts as counterparty liquidity to leveraged trading activity
on the exchange.

Yield comes from trading fees and counterparty PnL, not token emissions.
Traders pay fees when positions are opened and closed, and part of those
fees accrues to dfUSDC holders through the vault share price. Because the
vault is the counterparty to traders, it also captures net trader losses
over time, while net trader gains are paid from the vault.

Key features:

- ERC-4626 standard vault on Base
- Native USDC underlying asset
- Real-yield model driven by exchange activity
- Counterparty exposure to dominance perpetual markets

The dfUSDC vault does not charge a management fee or a performance fee to
depositors. There are no explicit deposit or withdrawal fees. Instead, the
vault is a yield-bearing ERC-4626 share whose dfUSDC to USDC exchange rate
reflects accumulated trading-fee revenue and net counterparty PnL.

How depositors earn:

- Traders pay a fee on notional volume when positions are opened and closed.
  The vault portion of those fees accrues to the vault and lifts the dfUSDC
  share price.
- The vault is the direct counterparty to leveraged traders. Net trader
  losses accrue to the vault, raising share price; net trader gains are paid
  out of the vault, lowering share price.

Mechanics (``DomfiVault.sol``):

- ``shareToAssetsPrice`` is the dfUSDC/USDC conversion rate. It rises with
  accrued fees and net trader losses and falls with net trader gains, so the
  reported share price is already net of the protocol's trading economics.
- ``accPnlPerTokenUsed`` tracks the vault's open and realised PnL per share
  and governs collateralisation.
- A daily PnL-outflow throttle rate-limits payouts to traders to protect
  depositors during stress.
- Optional deposit-with-lock methods can grant bonus shares to depositors
  who lock during under-collateralised periods. This is a depositor
  incentive, not a fee.

text: Ethena is a synthetic dollar protocol issuing USDe, backed by hedged crypto and stablecoin reserves, and sUSDe, its staked version that accrues protocol rewards.

[Ethena](https://ethena.fi/) is a synthetic dollar protocol that issues USDe and its staked,
yield-bearing version, sUSDe. Unlike a fiat-backed stablecoin, USDe is
[backed](https://docs.ethena.fi/overview/how-usde-works) by spot crypto hedged with short
perpetual and futures positions of about the same size, so the combined position is delta-neutral,
plus stablecoins and short-duration real-world assets that need no hedge. Its issuer is Ethena BVI
Limited, and the [USDe terms](https://docs.ethena.fi/resources/usde-terms-and-conditions) list
BTC, ETH, SOL, liquid staking tokens, USDC, USDT and USDtb among the reserves. Only whitelisted
counterparties that pass KYC checks can mint or redeem USDe directly; other holders trade it on
exchanges and onchain pools.

**sUSDe yield.** Staking USDe returns sUSDe, whose value in USDe rises as rewards are added to the
staking contract. Rewards are funded from
[protocol revenue](https://docs.ethena.fi/backing-assets/protocol-revenue): funding and basis
spreads on the hedges, overcollateralised DeFi and institutional lending, tokenised government
debt and credit, and stablecoin rewards. They are
[discretionary](https://docs.ethena.fi/protocol-overview/rewards-mechanism), paid by a subsidiary
of the Ethena Foundation, and never negative, as loss-making periods are meant to be absorbed by a
[reserve fund](https://docs.ethena.fi/protocol-overview/reserve-fund). The same revenue also funds
partner reward programmes.

**Unstaking and eligibility.** Unstaking starts a
[cooldown](https://docs.ethena.fi/video-guides/how-to-stake-usde) before USDe can be withdrawn,
currently one to seven days depending on reserve conditions and set by governance; exiting sooner
depends on secondary-market liquidity. sUSDe is not offered to residents of the EU or EEA, and the
[terms of service](https://docs.ethena.fi/resources/terms-of-service) bar US persons from Ethena's
app and services.

**Fees and risks.** Ethena does not currently charge fees for its app, although network fees
apply, and approved minters pay only execution costs such as gas when minting or redeeming USDe.
The main
[documented risks](https://docs.ethena.fi/protocol-overview/risks) are persistently negative
funding rates, liquidation of hedges, exchange failure, stablecoin depegs and the failure of the
[off-exchange custodians](https://docs.ethena.fi/overview/off-exchange-custody) that hold the
backing, currently Copper, Ceffu, Kraken and Anchorage Digital.

text:
[Euler](https://www.euler.finance/) is a modular, decentralised lending protocol built from
independent vaults. Each [vault](https://docs.euler.finance/learn/vaults/) lends one asset, such
as USDC, under its own settings, and vaults can accept deposits in other vaults as collateral, so
curators can build anything from isolated pairs to multi-asset lending markets. Euler v2
[launched in September 2024](https://www.euler.finance/blog/euler-q1-2026) and runs on
[Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Avalanche, BNB Chain, Monad, Plasma and other networks](https://docs.euler.finance/build/contract-addresses/).

**Vault types.** [Governed vaults](https://docs.euler.finance/learn/vault-types/) are managed by a
governor or risk curator who can change accepted collateral, loan-to-value limits, caps, oracles
and fees. Ungoverned vaults keep fixed parameters, and escrow vaults only hold collateral and earn
no interest. Euler Earn vaults take one asset and allocate it across Euler lending vaults and
other strategies chosen by their curator. Euler vault yields come from the interest borrowers
pay, minus any interest fee set by the vault's governor;
[Euler protocol fees have been zero since April 2026](https://docs.euler.finance/learn/interest-rates/).

**Withdrawals and risks.** Deposits are
[not principal-protected](https://docs.euler.finance/use/supply-assets/): a vault can lose value
through bad debt, oracle failure, smart contract failure or configuration changes, and
withdrawals are limited to liquidity that borrowers have not taken, so high utilisation can delay
them. Isolation contains losses rather than preventing them: when Stream Finance, which had
borrowed much of the liquidity on Euler's Plasma deployment, defaulted in late 2025, Euler Labs'
Q1 2026 review reported that the Plasma deployment was effectively wiped out, while Euler's
DAO-managed markets had no direct exposure.

**History.** Euler v1 was
[exploited for about $197 million in March 2023](https://www.euler.finance/blog/war-peace-behind-the-scenes-of-eulers-240m-exploit-recovery),
and all stolen funds were recovered within three weeks after negotiations with the attacker.
Euler v2 is a new codebase rebuilt from the ground up, and Euler publishes its
[security review and audit record](https://docs.euler.finance/security/).

[Hyperliquid](https://hyperliquid.xyz) is a layer 1 blockchain whose HyperCore layer runs
[fully onchain perpetual futures and spot order books](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs).
Hyperliquid vaults pool USDC that is traded on this exchange: depositors own a share of the vault
and take its profits and losses. These native HyperCore vaults were
[introduced in 2023](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/hypercore/vaults); the
documentation now calls them legacy vaults and points builders to tokenised vaults on HyperEVM.

**HLP.** The HLP vault, or
[Hyperliquidity Provider](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/hypercore/vaults/protocol-vaults),

liquidations and receives a portion of trading fees. Its
[liquidator vault](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/liquidations) takes
over positions that cannot be closed on the order book; these backstop liquidations are
profitable on average, but HLP carries the market risk of the positions it absorbs. HLP charges
no fees, and deposits can be withdrawn four days after the depositor's most recent deposit.

**User vaults.** Any trader can open a vault and trade perpetual futures with depositors' USDC;
these vaults cannot trade spot or builder-deployed (HIP-3) markets. The
[vault leader](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/hypercore/vaults/for-vault-leaders-legacy)
must keep at least 5% of the vault and receives 10% of depositors' profits. Returns depend on the
leader's trading, and past performance does not guarantee future returns.

**Withdrawals.** User vaults have a
[one-day lock-up after a deposit](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/hypercore/vaults/for-vault-depositors-legacy),
and the leader's profit share is deducted when depositors withdraw. If a vault lacks free margin,
open orders are cancelled and positions are closed in 20% steps until the withdrawal can be paid,
which can cause slippage. When a leader closes a vault, all positions are closed and depositors
receive their share.

Vault leaders receive a fixed 10% profit share from depositor profits, deducted
at withdrawal time. Protocol-managed vaults (e.g. HLP, HLP Strategy A/B) carry
no fees or profit sharing.

text:
IPOR Fusion uses the **internalised minting** fee mode. Both the management
fee and the performance fee are realised by minting new vault shares to
dedicated technical holding accounts, so fees are paid by existing share
holders through dilution. Investors do not pay any explicit fee at deposit
or redemption, and the share price reported by the vault is already
fees-net.

Fee caps (from ``PlasmaVaultLib.sol``):

- **Management fee**: up to 5% per year on assets under management
  (``MANAGEMENT_MAX_FEE_IN_PERCENTAGE = 500``, 2-decimal precision).
- **Performance fee**: up to 50% on gains above a high-water mark
  (``PERFORMANCE_MAX_FEE_IN_PERCENTAGE = 5000``).

Share-minting mechanism (``contracts/vaults/PlasmaVault.sol``):

- Every vault operation (deposit, mint, withdraw, redeem, execute,
  updateMarketsBalances) runs through fee hooks that call
  ``_realizeManagementFee()`` and ``_addPerformanceFee()``.
- ``_realizeManagementFee()`` (line 1413) — NatSpec: *"Realizes management
  fees by minting shares to fee recipient"*. Time-based accrual on
  ``grossTotalAssets`` is converted to shares via ``convertToShares()``
  and those shares are minted directly to ``MANAGEMENT_FEE_ACCOUNT``
  (``_mint(recipient, unrealizedFeeInShares)`` at line 1437). The
  management-fee timestamp is only updated after a successful mint
  (IL-6959 fix) to prevent fee suppression by many small transactions.
- ``_addPerformanceFee()`` (line 1381) — uses a high-water mark model. If
  ``totalAssetsAfter >= totalAssetsBefore``, the gain above the HWM is
  multiplied by the performance-fee rate, converted to shares by
  ``PlasmaVaultFeesLib.prepareForAddPerformanceFee()`` and minted
  (``_mint(recipient, feeShares)`` at line 1402). The HWM is stored in
  ``HighWaterMarkPerformanceFeeStorage`` and can be auto-lowered on a
  configurable update interval.
- Both mint paths temporarily disable ``totalSupplyCap`` validation so
  the fee mint cannot be blocked by the cap.

Downstream distribution (``contracts/managers/fee/FeeManager.sol``):

- ``harvestManagementFee()`` (line 194) and ``harvestPerformanceFee()``
  (line 247) read the already-minted share balances via
  ``IERC4626(PLASMA_VAULT).balanceOf(MANAGEMENT_FEE_ACCOUNT)`` and
  ``balanceOf(PERFORMANCE_FEE_ACCOUNT)``.
- ``_transferDaoFee()`` (line 636) moves the IPOR DAO portion via
  ``PLASMA_VAULT.transferFrom(feeAccount, daoRecipient, amount)``
  (line 650). ``_transferRecipientFee()`` (line 682) distributes the
  remainder to atomist-defined recipients using the same ``transferFrom``
  pattern (line 705).
- ``FeeAccount`` (``contracts/managers/fee/FeeAccount.sol``) is a tiny
  holding contract that only exposes ``approveMaxForFeeManager()`` so the
  ``FeeManager`` can pull the pre-minted shares — it never mints or burns
  anything itself.

Why this is internalised minting and not skimming or externalised:

- Skimming would transfer underlying assets out of the vault at the
  moment of profit. IPOR never moves assets for fees — it mints shares.
- Externalised fees (e.g. Lagoon) would deduct from the investor at
  redemption, so the vault share price is fees-gross. IPOR share price
  is fees-net: the dilution has already happened on-chain by the time
  ``totalAssets()`` / ``convertToAssets()`` are read.
- The ``FeeManager`` is a distribution layer on top of already-minted
  fee shares, not a separate fee-collection mechanism.

Optional deposit fee (per-vault add-on, usually 0):

- ``FeeManager.setDepositFee()`` (line 508) allows an atomist to
  configure an explicit deposit fee with 18-decimal precision. NatSpec
  says the fee is *"deducted from the user's deposit amount before
  minting shares"*, making it an externalised fee at deposit time. This
  is orthogonal to the management/performance fee mode and most Plasma
  Vaults leave it at 0.

Individual Plasma Vaults configure their own management and performance
percentages within the caps above.

text:
[Morpho](https://morpho.org/) is a decentralised, noncustodial lending protocol. Its
[lending markets](https://docs.morpho.org/learn/concepts/blue/) are isolated: each pairs one
collateral asset with one loan asset under a fixed liquidation loan-to-value and oracle, and
anyone can create one. Morpho vaults sit on top: a depositor supplies a single asset, such as
USDC or ETH, and the vault lends it across several markets. Morpho Blue and the first vaults
[went live at the start of 2024](https://morpho.org/blog/morpho-v2-liberating-the-potential-of-onchain-loans/),
and the contracts are
[deployed on Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum and more than 40 other networks](https://docs.morpho.org/developers/contracts/addresses/).

**Curators.** Each vault has a [curator](https://docs.morpho.org/learn/concepts/curator/) who
decides which markets it may lend to and caps its exposure to each, while allocators move
liquidity within those limits. Curator changes that add risk go through a timelock set for each
vault, which can give depositors time to exit before they apply.
[Morpho Vaults V2](https://morpho.org/blog/morpho-vaults-v2-a-new-standard-for-asset-curation/),
launched on 29 September 2025, can also allocate to other Morpho vaults and newer market types,
appoint sentinels who can cut risk in an emergency, and restrict deposits to approved users.

**Yield and fees.** Returns come from
[interest paid by borrowers](https://docs.morpho.org/developers/earn/concepts/yield-fees/) in the
underlying markets, so vault APYs move with borrowing demand. A vault can charge a
[performance fee](https://docs.morpho.org/curate/concepts/fee/) of up to 50% of the interest it
earns and, in V2, a management fee of up to 5% a year on deposits.

**Withdrawals and risks.** Exits depend on unborrowed liquidity in the markets a vault lends to,
so [high utilisation can delay withdrawals](https://docs.morpho.org/learn/resources/risks/). V2
vaults also let depositors redeem shares for the underlying market positions, subject to a penalty
of up to 2%, even when the vault lacks immediate liquidity. If collateral loses value faster than
liquidators can act,
[the bad debt is a loss for every lender in that market](https://docs.morpho.org/curate/tutorials-v1/bad-debt/),
including vaults allocated to it. Oracle failures and curator decisions are the other main risks;
Morpho publishes its [audit reports](https://docs.morpho.org/get-started/resources/audits/).

Morpho vaults can charge two fee types:

- **Performance fee**: Up to 50% of the interest the vault earns, taken when interest accrues
- **Management fee**: Up to 5% per year on total assets, available in Morpho Vaults V2 only

Fees are internalised into the share price through share minting to fee recipients.
Each vault sets its own fees: the owner does so in V1 vaults and the curator in V2 vaults. See
[Morpho vault fees](https://docs.morpho.org/curate/concepts/fee/).

[Sky](https://sky.money/), formerly MakerDAO, is the decentralised protocol behind the DAI and

to December 2017, and in September 2024 the protocol

[backed by](https://sky.money/blog/what-is-usds) stablecoin reserves, crypto-collateralised loans,

upgrade USDS to add a freeze function.

**Savings USDS and Savings DAI.** sUSDS earns the Sky Savings Rate, which SKY holders set through
onchain governance and which is funded by protocol revenue from collateralised loans, Treasury
bills and lending markets. The rate is variable and

DAI Savings Rate.

**Staked USDS.** [stUSDS](https://sky.money/stusds) is a higher-risk module that lends USDS to
borrowers who post staked SKY as collateral. It earns the SKY borrow rate on the lent share and
the Sky Savings Rate on the rest, so its yield moves with utilisation.
[Only USDS that is not lent out can be withdrawn](https://github.com/sky-ecosystem/stusds), so
exits can be delayed or partial when utilisation is high. Depositors take first-loss exposure: if
liquidations of SKY collateral fall short, stUSDS absorbs the bad debt, which ties its risk
closely to the SKY price. The stUSDS code also notes that depositors must trust Sky governance,
which can upgrade the contract.

text:
[YieldBasis](https://yieldbasis.com/) is a crypto protocol that lets people
put Bitcoin or Ethereum to work without giving up the usual up-and-down price
exposure of simply holding those assets. In a normal trading pool, liquidity
providers often end up worse off than if they had just held the coin, because
the pool automatically sells some of the asset as it rises and buys more as it
falls. YieldBasis is designed to avoid that drag: you deposit only the coin,
the protocol borrows a matching amount of a dollar-like stablecoin, and it
keeps the position balanced so your share still tracks the coin’s price
one-for-one while collecting trading fees.

In practice, depositors receive a token representing their share of that
position. They can either keep it and earn fees in Bitcoin or Ethereum terms,
or stake it to receive the protocol’s YB token instead. The idea is simple for
users—earn yield on BTC or ETH without the usual “impermanent loss”—but it
still carries real risks, including sharp price drops in the underlying asset,
delays when withdrawing after big market moves, and reliance on the stablecoin
and smart contracts that power the system. See the [YieldBasis overview](https://docs.yieldbasis.com/user/overview/how-yieldbasis-works)
and [Earn page](https://yieldbasis.com/earn) for current product terms.
